steps.title: Create message processing function
steps.instruction: Inside the main function, create a function named processMessage that takes a message object as a parameter and simulates processing it.
steps.hint: Define a function that will handle each message from your queue. You can use a function declaration or arrow function.
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have a processMessage function defined inside main, ready to simulate message processing.
successCriteria: The processMessage function is defined inside main and accepts a message parameter.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the processMessage function. This will be the core of your message processing logic.

steps.title: Add failure detection logic
steps.instruction: Inside the message processing function, add conditional logic to detect failed message processing based on message content or simulated errors. For example, check if a message contains an error flag or if processing fails after a certain number of retries.
steps.hint: You can simulate failure by checking if a message property (like 'hasError') is true, or by tracking retry counts. Use an if statement to detect these failure conditions.
steps.expectedOutcome: The message processing function now includes conditional logic to detect when message processing fails, which is essential for identifying messages that should be moved to the dead letter queue.
successCriteria: The processMessage function contains conditional logic (if statement) that checks for failure conditions such as error flags or retry limits.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added failure detection logic to your message processing function. This will help identify messages that need to be moved to the dead letter queue.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some logic, but make sure you're checking for specific failure conditions like error flags or retry limits. Add an if statement that detects when processing should fail.
steps.feedbackWrong: The failure detection logic is missing or incorrect. Inside processMessage, add conditional logic to detect failed message processing based on message content or simulated errors.

steps.title: Create dead letter queue handler
steps.instruction: Define a function named 'moveToDeadLetterQueue' that takes a failed message as a parameter and pushes it to the dead letter queue storage.
steps.hint: Inside the main function, create a new function that accepts a message parameter and uses the deadLetterQueue array's push method to add the message.
steps.expectedOutcome: A function named 'moveToDeadLetterQueue' is defined inside the main function, ready to handle failed messages by moving them to the dead letter queue.
successCriteria: The 'moveToDeadLetterQueue' function is defined with a message parameter and pushes the message to the deadLetterQueue array.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the dead letter queue handler function that will move failed messages to the dead letter queue storage.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've defined a function, but make sure it's named 'moveToDeadLetterQueue', accepts a message parameter, and pushes to the deadLetterQueue array.
steps.feedbackWrong: The dead letter queue handler function is not properly defined. It should be named 'moveToDeadLetterQueue', take a message parameter, and push to the deadLetterQueue array.

steps.title: Implement retry logic for failed messages
steps.instruction: Inside the processMessage function, add a retry counter and logic to retry processing up to 3 times before moving the message to the dead letter queue.
steps.hint: You can add a retryCount property to the message object or track retries separately. Use a loop or conditional checks to attempt processing multiple times.
steps.expectedOutcome: The processMessage function will now include retry logic that attempts to process messages multiple times before sending them to the dead letter queue.
successCriteria: The processMessage function contains retry logic with a maximum retry limit (e.g., 3 attempts) and properly moves messages to the dead letter queue after retries are exhausted.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully implemented retry logic. This will help handle temporary failures before messages are sent to the dead letter queue.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some retry logic, but make sure it has a clear maximum retry limit and properly moves messages to the dead letter queue when retries are exhausted.
steps.feedbackWrong: The retry logic appears to be missing or incomplete. Remember to add a retry counter and logic to attempt processing multiple times before moving messages to the dead letter queue.

steps.title: Create dead letter queue persistence
steps.instruction: Inside the main function, create a function named saveDeadLetterQueue that takes a message parameter and writes it to a file named 'dead-letter-queue.json' using the fs module's writeFileSync method.
steps.hint: You'll need to use fs.writeFileSync to write JSON data to a file. Remember to convert the message to a JSON string using JSON.stringify.
steps.expectedOutcome: A saveDeadLetterQueue function that writes message data to a file for persistent storage.
successCriteria: The saveDeadLetterQueue function is defined inside main, accepts a message parameter, and uses fs.writeFileSync to write JSON data to 'dead-letter-queue.json'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the persistence function that will save failed messages to disk.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your function uses fs.writeFileSync and writes JSON data to the correct filename.
steps.feedbackWrong: The persistence function isn't quite right. Check that you're using the fs module correctly and writing JSON data to the specified file.
